rows.selection_reason: 1) No prior evidence exists; the most critical uncertainty is whether any of the more complex design choices (multiprofile, transformer aggregation, multimodal fusion, learned encoders) actually improve over a simple baseline. 2) config_001 (RNA-only, single-profile, PCA n2000) is the simplest possible configuration and establishes a performance floor against which all subsequent experiments can be compared. It isolates the contribution of the RNA modality with a standard, well-understood linear representation. 3) Under a 10-experiment budget, anchoring with the simplest baseline first is the highest-information use of experiment 1: it lets every later result be interpreted as a delta over a known reference, and it prevents over-crediting complexity if a simple model already performs well. Subsequent experiments can then systematically test image-only, multimodal, alternative encoders, and aggregation strategies relative to this anchor.

1) Evidence: We have only one data point (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), which is a weak baseline. The most critical unknown is whether the image modality carries useful discriminative signal at all, since this determines whether multimodal fusion is worth pursuing or whether we should focus on improving RNA representations. 2) This experiment (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) directly tests image informativeness by switching only the modality while keeping the profile setting (singleprofile) and using a standard, well-established encoder. It is a clean single-variable comparison against the RNA baseline. 3) With 8 experiments remaining, resolving the modality question first is the highest-value use of the next slot: if image_only substantially outperforms 48.5%, we pivot to multimodal configs; if it is comparable or worse, we invest remaining budget in RNA encoder upgrades (scvi, scgpt) and multiprofile aggregation. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most consequential design axis.

Evidence: RNA (pca_n2000, singleprofile) achieves 0.485 accuracy while image (resnet50, singleprofile) is very weak at 0.208, indicating RNA is the dominant signal. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether the PCA linear encoder is the bottleneck for the RNA modality or whether the signal is simply limited. This experiment (config_004: rna_only, singleprofile, scvi_n200) makes a clean single-variable change from config_001, swapping only the RNA encoder from PCA to a learned nonlinear encoder (scvi_n200). If scvi significantly improves accuracy, it tells us the RNA representation is improvable and we should prioritize better encoders in subsequent experiments. If it does not improve, PCA is already near-optimal and we should shift focus to profile aggregation or multimodal fusion. With 7 experiments remaining, resolving whether the RNA encoder is the key lever is the highest-value uncertainty to reduce before committing to more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations.

Evidence: scvi_n200 (0.5203) clearly outperforms pca_n2000 (0.4849) for RNA singleprofile, establishing scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder so far. Image-only is very weak (0.2079), so multimodal gains are uncertain. Uncertainty: We have not yet tested whether multiprofile adds value over singleprofile with the best encoder. This experiment (config_005: rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) is a clean, single-variable comparison to config_004 (same encoder, singleprofile), isolating the effect of profile setting. If multiprofile helps, it opens a rich set of promising configurations for the remaining 6 experiments; if it does not, we can confidently focus budget on singleprofile variants (e.g., scgpt encoder or multimodal with a stronger image encoder). This is the highest-information experiment given the current sparse evidence and limited budget.

Evidence: config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) achieved the best accuracy so far (0.650), a large jump over singleprofile scvi_n200 (0.520) and pca_n2000 (0.485). Image-only models are weak (0.21), so RNA is the dominant signal. Uncertainty: within the multiprofile + scvi_n200 family, the only untested variable is aggregation method (transformer vs. avgpool). This experiment (config_006) isolates that single change, testing whether a transformer aggregator can further improve over avgpool. It is the best next step because it directly extends the current best result with a minimal, interpretable change, and the outcome (whether transformer > avgpool) will inform all subsequent multimodal experiments where aggregation is a key design choice. With 5 experiments remaining, establishing the optimal aggregation before moving to multimodal fusion is the most efficient use of budget.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 acc. Multiprofile + scvi_n200 is a large jump over singleprofile (0.653 vs 0.520), and transformer vs avgpool makes negligible difference (0.653 vs 0.650). Image alone is very weak (0.208). Uncertainty: We have not yet tested whether scgpt, a different RNA foundation model encoder, could outperform scvi_n200 in the multiprofile setting. This experiment (config_009: rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, transformer) is a clean single-variable change from our best result, isolating the encoder effect. It is the best use of this slot because: (1) if scgpt improves over scvi_n200, we identify a stronger backbone to build multimodal models on in the remaining 4 experiments; (2) if it does not, we confirm scvi_n200 is optimal and can confidently allocate remaining budget to multimodal fusion experiments with the known-best encoder. This reduces the most important remaining uncertainty (encoder choice) before committing budget to more complex multimodal configurations.

The current best is config_006 (RNA-only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 acc. The RNA-only design space is well-characterized: scvi_n200 is the best encoder, multiprofile gives a large boost, and transformer aggregation marginally beats avgpool. The critical open question is whether adding the image modality (via fusion) can improve beyond 0.653, even though image-only performance is weak (0.208). config_032 extends config_006 by adding resnet50 image features with concat fusion while keeping all other settings identical, cleanly isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. This is the highest-value experiment because the answer determines the strategy for the remaining 3 runs: if fusion helps, we can refine (weighted fusion, ViT); if it hurts, we confirm RNA-only as the ceiling and avoid wasting budget on further multimodal variants.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.6878 acc. The strongest evidence shows scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer aggregation is the optimal RNA-side setup, and adding image via concat fusion provides a ~3.5% boost over RNA-only. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the fusion strategy (concat vs. weighted) can further improve performance. config_033 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted, isolating that single variable. This is the best use of experiment 8 because: (1) it is a minimal, interpretable extension of the current best, (2) if weighted fusion improves accuracy, the final experiment can combine it with a stronger image encoder (config_039, ViT-L + weighted), and (3) if it does not improve, we confirm concat is optimal and the final experiment can test ViT-L with concat (config_038) to probe whether a stronger image encoder adds value. Either outcome maximally informs the last experiment.

The current best is config_033 (scvi_n200 + resnet50, multiprofile, transformer, weighted) at 0.713. The image-only ResNet50 baseline was very weak (0.208), suggesting the image encoder may be a bottleneck in the multimodal fusion. Config_039 swaps only the image encoder to ViT-L (imagenet_vit_l) while keeping the proven-best RNA encoder (scvi_n200), profile (multiprofile), aggregation (transformer), and fusion (weighted, which outperformed concat by ~2.5pp). This isolates the effect of image representation quality. If ViT-L provides a stronger visual embedding, it could push accuracy above 0.713; if not, we retain 0.713 as our best. This is the highest-value single change to test with one experiment remaining, as it directly extends the winning configuration along the most uncertain axis (image encoder strength) without introducing multiple simultaneous changes.

Evidence: The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250. All component choices in config_039 are supported by ablations: scvi_n200 > scgpt > pca for RNA, imagenet_vit_l > resnet50 for image, multiprofile > singleprofile, transformer > avgpool, and weighted > concat (0.7131 vs 0.6878 with resnet50). Question: config_038 is identical to config_039 except it uses concat fusion instead of weighted. While weighted outperformed concat by ~0.025 with resnet50, the interaction with the stronger imagenet_vit_l backbone could shift the balance—concat might preserve complementary information that weighted averaging dilutes. Why this is the best use of the final experiment: With 0 experiments remaining, exploitation is paramount. config_038 shares 5 of 6 design axes with the current best and is the highest-expected-value untested configuration. All other remaining options swap the RNA encoder to scgpt or pca (both substantially worse in RNA-only) or drop to singleprofile, making them very unlikely to exceed 0.7250. config_038 offers the best (albeit modest) chance of a small improvement or at minimum a clean confirmation of the optimal fusion strategy.
